I can't imagine a world without him. He loves how much more alike we get as we get older. He constantly says it with a big smile on his face. Occasionally, his bad communication skills are very apparent and his disorder is obvious in other ways as well. I feel if I tell my brother I have Aspberger's as well he would learn to love it and not deny it anymore, possibly helping himself. Would I be an asshole if I live a lie for the rest of my life to make my brother feel he's not alone and possibly help him move forward in life?

Preparing the turkey for the first time can be a bit daunting, especially when there's a family recipe involved. Make sure to get all the details, including ingredient quantities, cooking methods, and any special instructions. 2. **Read and understand the recipe**: Go through the recipe carefully and make sure you understand each step. Measure ingredients accurately, and use the correct cooking techniques and temperatures. 6. **Don't be afraid to ask for help**: If you're unsure about any part of the recipe or encounter any issues during cooking, don't hesitate to ask a family member for guidance. 7. **Be prepared for variables**: Keep in mind that cooking a turkey can be affected by various factors, such as the size of the bird, the oven temperature, and the altitude. Be prepared to make adjustments if needed. 8. **Use a meat thermometer**: To ensure the turkey is cooked to a safe internal temperature (165°F), use a meat thermometer. This will help you avoid overcooking or undercooking the bird. 9. **Let it rest**: Once the turkey is cooked, let it rest for about 30 minutes before carving. This will help the juices redistribute, making the meat more tender and flavorful. 10. **Relax and enjoy**: Remember that it's okay to make mistakes, and the most important thing is to enjoy the time with your family. Take a deep breath, relax, and savor the experience of cooking the turkey for the first time.
